compiled_state.title: As an operator, /debug-everything Phase F (Tier 0-1 tool-atomic auto-fix) commits each tier as a single coherent sub-branch when running in ci-pr mode
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Add Phase F sub-branch logic that produces one sub-branch per tool-atomic tier (Tier 0 = `make format`, Tier 1 = `ruff --fix`) rather than chunking by bug count.

**Why**: Tool-atomic tiers produce one atomic commit per tier; 5-bug chunking would create empty commits and orchestrator thrash for these tiers.

**Scope**:
- IN: When `merge.strategy=pr`, Phase F creates exactly one sub-branch per active tier (`bug-batch/<debug-session-id>/tier-0` and `bug-batch/<debug-session-id>/tier-1`); when a tier has zero applicable bugs, no sub-branch is created and the aggregate PR is not annotated for that tier; co-locate sub-branch creation instructions in the Phase F section header (not in cross-mode preamble).
- OUT: Phase G sub-branch logic (S5); leak detection (S9); DEBUG_BRANCH_TRACKING comment (S7).

## Done Definitions

- When complete, /debug-everything Phase F in ci-pr mode produces exactly one sub-branch per applicable tier (`tier-0`, `tier-1`) with no per-bug count chunking
  ← Satisfies: "Phase F (Tier 0-1 tool-atomic auto-fix) produces exactly one sub-branch per tier with no per-bug count chunking"
- When complete, when a Phase F tier has zero applicable bugs, no sub-branch is created and no aggregate-PR annotation is added for that tier
  ← Satisfies: "Phase F (Tier 0-1 tool-atomic auto-fix) produces exactly one sub-branch per tier"
- When complete, Phase F sub-branch instructions are co-located in the Phase F section header of `debug-everything/SKILL.md` (not in a cross-mode preamble)
  ← Satisfies: "Mechanism applies to Bug-Fix Mode, Phase F, Phase G with instructions co-located in each mode's section header"
- Unit tests written and passing covering zero-bug-tier, one-bug-tier, and many-bug-tier cases
  ← Satisfies: "Phase F produces exactly one sub-branch per tier"

## Considerations

- [Testing] Zero-bug-tier case is non-obvious and must be explicitly tested; missing this test could let S12's ≥3 sub-branch acceptance pass with empty branches

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
